Hash Generator

A hash function turns any text or file into a fixed-length fingerprint: change one character and the hash changes completely. The SHA-256 hash of hello world is b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9. To check a download, choose the file and paste the checksum from the website: the tool tells you if it matches.

Drop a file here or click to choose Any file · it’s read on your device, never uploaded

Your files are processed on your device and never uploaded.

What a hash is

A cryptographic hash function takes input of any size and produces a fixed-size output, usually shown in hexadecimal. Good hash functions have three key properties:

  • Deterministic: the same input always gives the same hash.
  • Avalanche effect: a tiny change (one letter, one bit) gives a completely different hash.
  • One-way: you can't work backwards from a hash to the original input, and it's infeasible to find two inputs with the same hash.

Which algorithm?

AlgorithmLengthStatus
MD5128 bits (32 hex)Broken for security: collisions are easy to create. Fine for spotting accidental corruption.
SHA-1160 bits (40 hex)Broken for security since 2017. Still used by Git for object IDs.
SHA-256256 bits (64 hex)Secure. The standard choice for checksums, certificates and blockchains.
SHA-384384 bits (96 hex)Secure; a shortened SHA-512.
SHA-512512 bits (128 hex)Secure, and often faster than SHA-256 on 64-bit computers.

Verifying a download

  1. On the download page, find the checksum (often labelled SHA-256, SHA256SUMS or "checksum").
  2. Choose File above and select the downloaded file.
  3. Paste the checksum into Expected hash. A green "Match" means the file is exactly the one the publisher released, not damaged in transfer or swapped.

The same check from a terminal:

Windows: certutil -hashfile file.iso SHA256 macOS: shasum -a 256 file.iso Linux: sha256sum file.iso

Hashing text

Text is converted to bytes using UTF-8 before hashing, the same as most programming languages and command-line tools. Hidden differences such as a trailing space or newline change the hash, so if your result doesn't match another tool's, check for those. For example, echo "hello world" | sha256sum includes a newline; printf "hello world" doesn't.

Don't store passwords with these hashes

MD5 and SHA hashes are designed to be fast, which makes them unsuitable for passwords: attackers can try billions of guesses per second. Use a dedicated password hashing function such as Argon2, bcrypt or scrypt, which are slow on purpose and add a unique salt to each password.

Everything is computed in your browser with the built-in Web Crypto API (and the CryptoJS library for MD5). Your text and files never leave your device.

Frequently asked questions

How do I get the SHA-256 hash of a file?

Choose File, then select the file. Its SHA-256 hash appears along with MD5, SHA-1, SHA-384 and SHA-512.

How do I verify a checksum?

Select the file and paste the published checksum into Expected hash. The tool tells you whether it matches.

Is MD5 still safe?

Not for security, because collisions can be created on purpose. It is still fine for detecting accidental corruption.

Can a hash be reversed?

No. Hashes are one-way. Short or common inputs can sometimes be guessed by trying many possibilities, which is why passwords need special slow hashes.

Are my files uploaded?

No. Hashes are calculated in your browser, so files never leave your device.
